title: Reimagine Your Boss as Customer
author: Kurt Mueller
summary: Kurt Mueller argues that employees can strengthen their standing, and their resilience through organizational change, by treating their boss as a primary customer. He lists the benefits as a broader view of strategy, sharper focus on high-value work, and more proactive problem-solving. He then names the obstacles, including personal friction, competing priorities and the power imbalance of a command-and-control boss, and suggests treating the boss as the most important but not the only customer. The practical core is a set of habits: regular goal-alignment check-ins, proactive updates, bringing solutions with problems, and matching the boss's communication style. The piece is a compact, if loosely edited, managing-up primer whose through-line is that loyalty and trust come from understanding the other person's needs and pressures.
points: Managing up is framed as career insurance: a boss who trusts you is the best protection in times of organizational change or economic uncertainty.
Understanding the boss's objectives and KPIs gives a clearer view of how your own role fits the organization's mission.
Mueller admits the customer metaphor can be a step too far for some, and offers adapting to communication style and resolving conflict promptly as lighter alternatives.
The concrete habits are regular alignment check-ins, concise proactive updates, and presenting well-thought-out solutions alongside problems.
quotes: In times of organizational change or economic uncertainty, having the support and trust of your boss can be crucial. It positions you as a reliable and valuable contributor to the the bosses success, which can be beneficial for your long-term career resilience.

Feeling more of a sense of dependency than a customer-service provider dynamic due to the power imbalance. This is particularly difficult to overcome if working for a boss with a “command and control.” leadership style.
Conduct regular check-ins and goal alignment sessions to understand your boss’s strategic priorities. This can help you ensure that your efforts support what they hope to accomplish.
Provide regular updates and anticipate information needs. Proactive communication keeps your boss informed, builds trust and ensures never being caught off guard by unexpected developments.

Demonstrate initiative and problem-solving support. Identify problems with proposed solutions before they escalate. By independently demonstrating your capability and reliability, you will reduce your boss’s workload.

Matching your your communication style. By taking steps to adapt your communication style to reflect the boss’s preferences you will increase confidence that you understand their needs wants and desires.

Just like building relationships with actual service or product customers, loyalty is developed by gaining a deep understanding of his or her needs wants and desires. You must strive to understand your bosses world that includes pressures faced; personal as well as organizational objectives and expectations from his or her own boss and peers.
